## 6. Business logic implemented in the frontend mock

These rules live in `web/src/mock/handlers.ts` and `web/src/mock/ai/*`. Whatever replaces the mock must keep them (in the backend, the adapter or the sidecar).

### 6.1 Permissions
- Only the case **owner or a co-owner** (or the head) changes a case; everyone can read, comment, watch, escalate. Only the requirement owner (or head) edits it.
- **Head of product line** (`role = head`) sends back, signs off, resolves escalations, edits the brand profile and default weight profiles.
- Series PMs (plan `ownerIds`) edit the vehicle plan.

### 6.2 Case lifecycle (frontend)
- States: `observed → new → investigating → awaiting_answers → ready → decided`. Actions `open`, `start`, `await`, `ready`, `reopen` move the state; every move needs a rationale.
- Deciding sets `state = decided` and an **outcome**: `confirm` (drafts requirements via the requirement agent if none exist), `refer` (to another PM: creates a `Referral`, the receiver becomes a watcher and is notified), `innovation` (adds to the pool with a horizon and the PM's pitch), `park`, `reject`, `merge` (moves signals into the target, recomputes its figures, notifies the target owner).
- `refer` with `escalate: true` creates an **escalation** to the head instead (anyone involved may escalate, e.g. China vs. rest-of-world conflict).
- Every decision is prepended to the case page's "Decision log" and audited.
- Referral decisions: `accept` creates a **linked case** in the receiver's workspace (`originCaseId`), `decline` puts the source case back to `ready`, `escalate` hands it to the head, `resolve` (head) records a resolution (one market, market variant, keep both, take over, return) in the case context and decision log.

### 6.3 Requirement lifecycle (frontend)
`draft → in_discussion → pm_approved → signed_off → planned → exported`, plus `rejected` (restore → `draft`).
- `approve` (owner, from draft or in discussion) notifies the head with a sign-off request; the open quality-check issues are recorded in the audit event (section 6.9).
- `send_back` (head, from pm_approved) → `in_discussion` with `sentBackReason`, owner notified.
- `sign_off` (head, from pm_approved) → owner notified.
- `plan` (owner/head, from signed_off) links or creates a `PlannedFeature` in the series plan.
- `export` (from planned); the Codebeamer export also moves every planned requirement to `exported`.
- IDs: `REQ-<series>-NNNN`, China variants `REQ-<series>-CN-NNNN`.

### 6.4 Scoring (reference, `mock/scoring.ts`)
- Factors (all 0..1): `customers`, `severity`, `satisfaction_gap`, `competitor_gap`, `market_volume`, `regression`, `trend`, `brand_fit`.
- `case score = Σ w_f · factor_f / Σ w_f` (no cost). `requirement score = case score × costMultiplier[size]`.
- Manual ranks (with reason) win over the computed order. Observed, rejected and merged cases are not ranked.
- `previewScores` re-ranks with unsaved weights; the UI shows "moved because…" and a robustness column (stays in the top 5 under every profile).
- `customers` is recomputed from the case's signals: `log10(1 + n) / log10(61)`.

### 6.5 AI assistant (`mock/ai/chat.ts`, scripted unless a key is set)
Intent by message text; every answer cites evidence as `[SIGNAL-ID]`, and every change is a proposal:
- "research …" → mock research run adds two synthetic web signals to the case (audited as `agent:researcher`).
- "draft a SMART requirement" → `new_requirement` proposal(s) from `ai/drafts.ts`.
- "what should I ask engineering/finance" → `new_question` proposals.
- "why is this ranked so high", "compare the markets", "what do competitors offer", "argument sheet", "set the target to …" (field proposal) → cited answers.
- Free-form questions go to the live LLM when available (context: case, figures, up to 40 signals, page, requirement).
- `savePmContext` stores the PM's market focus, cost sensitivity, positioning, timing and note in the case context, then the assistant posts 1 to 2 follow-up questions the data cannot answer (market mismatch, platform change vs. LCI, paid option vs. standard, match/beat competitors).
- `addMeetingNote` (`ai/notes.ts`) extracts answers to open questions, field updates and decision-log entries from pasted notes as proposals.
- Proposal kinds: `field`, `body`, `question_answer`, `new_question`, `new_requirement`. Accepting applies the change, logs a context entry and an audit event.

### 6.6 Monitoring and refresh
- `refresh` runs once over a pool of authored web findings: new signals attach to their case, owners and watchers are notified, a competitor fact with a metric raises an **alert** ("raises the bar") on the case; a second run finds nothing (dedupe by URL and content hash). An `AgentRun` is recorded.
- `resolveAlert`: dismiss, or `rework` (requirement back to in_discussion, case back to investigating).

### 6.7 Vehicle plan and export
- The plan lists features per car area with today's availability (standard/optional/absent/removed), action (keep/new/improve/remove), release, protected flag and linked requirements.
- Codebeamer CSV columns: ID, Summary, Description, Category, Market, Release, Priority, Score, Evidence level, Metrics, Acceptance criteria, Assumptions, Cost size, Cost band, Linked case, Linked findings, Rationale, Status. Sorted by rank under the user's weight profile.

### 6.8 Engineering deck (`requirementDeck` + `web/src/lib/deck.ts`)
Signed-off, planned and exported requirements of a series, sorted by rank. Per slide: SMART text and metrics, top 3 BMW complaint quotes (not likes), score breakdown (factor value × normalized weight), competitor gap, last 5 decisions (requirement and case), open quality issues. Rendered client-side with `pptxgenjs`. Easy to rebuild on real data: it only needs requirement, case factors + weights, case signals and decisions.

### 6.9 Quality check (`mock/ai/quality.ts`)
Runs automatically after drafting and every edit, and on demand. Warns, never blocks; approving lists the open issues and requires a reason.
- `vague_word` (title, description, acceptance criteria: "improved", "better", "user-friendly", "intuitive", "seamless", …; red if no metric has a numeric target).
- `missing_scope` (scope global while > 80 % of the case's verbatims come from one market; China scope with < 3 Chinese verbatims).
- `out_of_scope` (homologation, type approval, UN-R, ISO 26262, emissions, crash test, ECU, CAN bus, supplier, part number, price/pricing, business case) — red.
- `duplicate` (≥ 30 % word overlap with a live requirement of the same series, red) / `baukasten` (same in another series, or the case spans several series, amber, suggests the cross-series PM).
- `conflict` (same metric question with another target in the same car area; or relies on a feature the plan removes).
- Optional LLM pass adds issues of the same kinds (strict JSON, related IDs validated).
Portable as-is: inputs are a requirement, its case figures, all requirements and the plan. Could later move to Python next to `requirements/service.py`.

### 6.10 Ask the segment (`mock/ai/segment.ts`)
- Segments = markets of the case (+ market × powertrain with ≥ 3 verbatims), counted **only from real BMW verbatims** (no synthetic, no web).
- With verbatims: counts by kind + 3 to 5 strongest quotes, cited. Live LLM gets only that segment's quotes and must summarize in the third person; citations not in the set are dropped.
- Without verbatims: "No evidence for China owners", the closest segment with data, and a `new_question` proposal to the market PM. Never a guess.
- On real data: segments come from `GET /signals?case_id=…` filtered by `evidence_role = bmw_customer` (or `source_id = bmw_feedback`), grouped by `market` and `powertrain`.

### 6.11 Audit actions written by the mock
`case.created/edited/state_changed/decided/pm_context_saved/exported_md`, `requirement.drafted/edited/status_changed/checked/deck_exported`, `requirements.exported`, `proposal.accepted/rejected/created`, `question.created/answered/edited`, `meeting_note.added`, `referral.*`, `escalation.*`, `alert.*`, `plan.feature_*`, `signals.fetched/researched`, `segment.asked`, `comment.added`, `weight_profile.*`, `brand_profile.updated`, `workspace.updated`. Actor = user id or `agent:<name>`.

## 7. The backend on `main` (what exists)

**Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, psycopg, Supabase Postgres + pgvector (local embedded Postgres for dev), OpenAI (chat + embeddings; key still missing → offline fallbacks), `uv`.

**Run:**
```bash
cd backend
cp .env.example .env          # Supabase URL/keys or leave empty for local; AUTH_MODE=dev for X-User-Id
uv run python -m app.demo build --fresh   # local DB: migrate, seed, cases, scores, RAG, demo users (~10 min)
uv run python -m app.demo users           # prints demo user ids
uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload      # http://localhost:8000/docs
```
CORS already allows `http://localhost:3000`.

**Auth:** `AUTH_MODE=dev` → header `X-User-Id: <app_user uuid>`; production → `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase JWT>`. Demo users (fixed ids):
`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` Demo PM 5 Series (`pm`, `[G60]`), `…0002` PM 7 Series (`[G70]`), `…0003` PM 1 Series (`[F70]`), `…0004` engineer, `…0005` admin. Roles: `pm`, `engineer`, `admin`; a PM acts only on the lines in `app_user.vehicles` (empty = all).

**Core concepts that differ from the frontend:**
- **Config** = one PM view: vehicle × market (`G60 / USA`). Each config has several **weight profiles**; scores and ranks exist **per profile**. Boards always need `profile_id`.
- **Case is not tied to one vehicle**: `case_item` (topic + aspect group, page `body_md` with `body_version`, figures per vehicle × market × powertrain, brand fit, segment) and `case_vehicle` (per line: state `observed | open | confirmed | rejected`, opened-by rule, market conflict, release fit, manual rank, new-evidence flag). Case IDs `CASE-0012`.
- **Requirement** is a page: `title`, `body_md` (+ version, stale saves → 409), `metric_target` (jsonb), `acceptance_criteria`, `assumptions`, `release_target` (`next_gen | current_car | ota`), `evidence_level` (`bmw_data | web | assumption`), `cost_size` + `cost_source`, status `draft | in_discussion | approved | rejected | deleted` (tombstone). IDs `REQ-G60-0012` (number = case number), `REQ-G60-USA-0012` when split per market. Generated when the PM confirms the case for a line.
- **Scoring:** factors `distinct_customers, severity, satisfaction_gap, competitor_gap, market_volume, removed_vs_predecessor, reach, trend`; `score = brand_multiplier × Σ w·f / Σ w` (brand fit is a **multiplier** `fits 1.0 / neutral 0.8 / off_brand 0.5`, not a factor); requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (`S 1.0, M 0.85, L 0.7`; missing cost = 1.0). Manual ranks first; `score_moved` flag when a score changes by ≥ 0.1.
- **RAG sidebar agent:** hybrid search (full text + pgvector), tools `search_signals, get_case, get_requirement, score_breakdown, compare_markets, what_if_weights, propose_edit`; citations `[signal:<uuid>]` must have been retrieved, else "No evidence found in the stored sources."; edits are a proposed page diff accepted via `/chat/messages/{id}/decision`.
- **Signals:** uuid ids, `record_id` → `source_record` (exact quote checkable), `evidence_role` (`bmw_customer | competitor | market`), `kind`, `severity`, topic (`feature`), `aspect_group`, `car_area[]`, `market` (`USA | China | Europe | Rest of World | unknown`), `powertrain`, `scope_tag`, `validation` (`valid | quarantined | deleted`).
- **Audit:** `audit_event` append-only (`actor` like `pm:<uuid>`, `agent:rag`, `seed:…`), `decision` table for PM actions, `page_version` for page history, `log_access` for views and exports.

**Endpoints (about 50):** see the table in `backend/API.md`. Highlights the UI does not use yet: case page versions and stale-save protection, merge/split, tag overrides (brand fit, segment, release fit), predecessor research, profile compare (robust top N), config source filter, quarantine release/delete, taxonomy review queue, audit chain report per requirement, overview map per line, signal detail with its source record.

### 8.2 Feature coverage

| Area | Backend has it | Missing on the backend (needs sidecar or a backend extension) |
|---|---|---|
| Signals, quarantine, taxonomy, runs | yes | trigger a fetch run from the UI (`refresh`), `trust` tier, `agent` label |
| Case board, page, scores | yes (per profile) | owner / co-owners / watchers, the finer workflow states (investigating, awaiting answers, ready), outcomes refer / innovation / park, `highlights`, PM context, create a case from loose signals, what-if preview endpoint |
| Requirements | yes (page-based) | structured SMART fields edit (`metrics[]` with basis/benchmark, acceptance criteria, assumptions, marketScope) as an endpoint; head sign-off, plan and export statuses; send back reason; owner |
| Chat | yes (RAG, cited, page diffs) | proposals other than page diffs (new question, new requirement, field), research runs, PM-context follow-ups, segment mode |
| Collaboration | notifications, decisions, audit per object | users list, open questions, meeting notes, referrals and escalations, innovation pool, comments + mentions, alerts with resolve, global audit list, search |
| Vehicle plan | today's equipment in `vehicle_feature` | plan features (action, protected, release), plan endpoints, Codebeamer CSV in the UI's column set, deck payload |
| Quality check, segments | — | both (frontend logic is portable, section 6.9 / 6.10) |

### 8.3 Options

1. **Adapter / BFF in Next.js (recommended).** Keep the UI and its contract. Add backend-backed handlers next to the mock handlers, same `Handlers` type, choose per endpoint. UI-only collaboration objects live in a sidecar store keyed by real backend IDs. Pros: zero UI churn, contract test still guards the shapes, instant fallback to the mock for the demo, backend unchanged. Cons: mapping code; sidecar is in-memory until persisted.
2. **Implement the frontend contract in FastAPI** (a new `ui` router that serves `contracts/openapi.yaml`, plus tables for the missing features). Cleanest long-term, everything audited in Postgres; more Python work and riskier before a demo.
3. **Rewrite the UI against `backend/API.md`.** Most churn; loses features the backend lacks.

A good path: start with option 1 now, and move pieces into the backend (option 2) when they stabilize (users list, statuses, structured requirement patch, questions, referrals).

### 8.4 Step-by-step plan (option 1)

**Step 0 — Branch and run both.**
- Merge PR #5 (or merge `main` into `feature/frontend-demo` again: `main` gained phases 7 to 10 after the PR was opened). Work on a new branch `feature/integration`.
- Run the backend locally (`AUTH_MODE=dev`, `python -m app.demo build --fresh`, uvicorn on :8000) and the web app (:3000).

**Step 1 — Plumbing.**
- `web/.env.local`: `DATA_SOURCE=backend`, `BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000`.
- New folder `web/src/backend/`:
  - `client.ts`: server-side `fetch` to `BACKEND_URL` with `X-User-Id` (or Bearer), JSON errors → `ApiError(status, detail)` (FastAPI errors are `{detail}`).
  - `map.ts`: all vocabulary mappings of 8.1, in both directions, unit-tested.
  - `handlers.ts`: `Partial<Handlers>` implemented against the backend.
  - `sidecar.ts`: in-memory store for UI-only objects (questions, meeting notes, PM context, referrals, innovation, plan features, comments, alerts, proposals of non-diff kinds, owner/workflow state, quality checks), keyed by backend IDs; reuse `mock/store.ts` helpers.
- `route.ts`: pick `backendHandlers[name] ?? mockHandlers[name]` when `DATA_SOURCE=backend`; keep the mock as the default.

**Step 2 — Read path (what the screens show).**

- `cases`: `GET /cases?profile_id=<workspace profile>&state=observed&state=open&state=confirmed&state=rejected` → map each board row to a full `Case` (fill fields the board lacks with defaults or a per-case `GET /cases/{id}` when needed; owner from sidecar, default = the persona of the config). `figures.perMarket` from `markets` (customers, negative share).

- `weightProfiles`: profiles of the persona's config (`GET /configs`), factor names mapped; `brand_fit` slider ↔ brand multipliers (decision needed, 8.5).
- `audit`: per object → `GET /audit/{object_type}/{object_id}` (map `actor` `pm:<uuid>` → persona id); global list → needs a backend endpoint (or merge per-object calls for the current case and requirements).
- `brandProfile`: backend `body_md` → `notesMd`; pillars from the sidecar or parsed headings.

**Step 3 — Write path.**
- `transitionCase`: `confirm | reject | reopen | open` → `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{vehicle}/transition` (vehicle = the persona's line); `merge` → `POST /cases/{id}/merge {target_id, rationale}` (backend refuses cross-topic merges); `start | await | ready | refer | innovation | park` and escalations → sidecar (backend state stays `open`). After confirm, the backend returns the generated requirement ids.
- `generateRequirements` → `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{vehicle}/requirements`.
- `patchCase`: `bodyMd`/`title` → `PUT /cases/{id}/page` with `expected_version = bodyVersion` (409 → toast "someone saved first, reload"); `brandFit` → `POST /cases/{id}/tags {field: "brand_fit", …}` (map 0..1 → fits/neutral/off_brand); `manualRank` → `POST …/vehicles/{v}/rank`; watchers / co-owners → sidecar.
- `transitionRequirement`: `discuss` → status `in_discussion`, `approve` → `approved`, `reject` → `rejected`, `restore` → `draft`; `send_back | sign_off | plan | export` → sidecar layer on top of backend `approved` (or extend the backend status flow, 8.5).
- `patchRequirement`: `releaseTarget` → `/retarget`, `cost.size` → `/cost`, `manualRank` → `/rank`, everything else (title, description, metrics, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope) → render into `body_md` and `PUT /page` with the version, or add a structured PATCH on the backend (preferred, 8.5).
- `postMessage` (no segment) → `POST /chat/{type}/{id} {question}`; map the agent row to `ChatMessage` (rewrite `[signal:<uuid>]` to `[<uuid>]` and fill `citations` from `cited_signals`); a `proposed_diff` becomes a `Proposal { kind: "body", id: <message id> }`. `decideProposal` on such an id → `POST /chat/messages/{id}/decision {accept}`; other proposal kinds stay in the sidecar/scripted flow.
- `postMessage` with `segment` and `caseSegments`: compute in the adapter from the case's real signals (port of `mock/ai/segment.ts`).
- `exportRequirements`: map to `GET /requirements/export?profile_id=…&format=csv` or build the UI's Codebeamer CSV from the requirements (the backend export is "approved top N" only; it logs the export in `decision` and `audit_event` either way).
- Weight profiles: `createWeightProfile` → `POST /configs/{id}/profiles`, `saveWeightProfile` → `PATCH /profiles/{id}`; `previewScores` → recompute in the adapter from stored factor values (`score = brand × Σ w·f / Σ w`) or add a backend preview endpoint.

**Step 4 — UI-only features on real data (sidecar).**
Open questions, meeting notes (+ `ai/notes.ts`), PM context (+ follow-ups), referrals / escalations, innovation pool, comments + mentions, alerts, vehicle plan (seed today's equipment from backend `vehicle_feature` once an endpoint exists), quality check (`ai/quality.ts` on mapped requirements), deck (`requirementDeck` on mapped data), search (combine backend board `q` and sidecar). Persist the sidecar later as backend tables (option 2).

**Step 5 — Verify.**
- `npm run contract-test` with `API_BASE=http://localhost:3000/api` and `DATA_SOURCE=backend` (parametrize the IDs: pick the first open case and a confirmed one from the board instead of `CASE-G60-0001`).
- Backend: `uv run pytest` and `uv run python -m app.demo e2e "G60 / USA"`.
- Click through the demo storyline with real data; check the audit trail shows backend events (actor `pm:<uuid>`).

### 8.5 Decisions the team must make

1. **Which data source per screen for the demo** (real where it exists, sidecar for the rest, or full mock as fallback)? Recommendation: real for signals, cases, scores, requirements, chat, audit; sidecar for collaboration.
2. **Persona ↔ backend user ↔ config mapping** (8.4 step 1). Do we keep the six named personas on real data?
3. **Requirement statuses:** extend the backend flow with `signed_off` (head) and `planned`/`exported`, or keep them as a frontend layer? Recommendation: extend the backend (two statuses + who may set them), small change in `requirements/service.py` and the check constraint.
4. **Structured requirement editing:** add `PATCH /requirements/{id}` for metrics, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope (audited like the rest), or keep editing the page markdown only?
5. **Brand fit:** factor (frontend) or multiplier (backend)? Recommendation: follow the backend (multiplier); the weights panel hides the `brand_fit` slider and shows the brand-fit tag instead; add `reach` as a slider.
6. **Case workflow:** do the frontend sub-states (investigating, awaiting answers, ready) and outcomes (refer, innovation pool, park) become backend concepts? Recommendation: store them in the sidecar first; later a `case_vehicle.workflow` column + `referral` and `innovation` tables.
7. **Chat:** backend RAG agent for free-form questions (OpenAI key needed), keep the scripted flows (draft requirement, questions for engineering, segment mode) in the adapter?
8. **Which ID the UI shows for signals:** uuid, or the readable `record_id` (`bmw_feedback-G60-0001`, matching the old `G60-0001` style)?

---

## 9. Gotchas

- **Scale.** The mock has 28 cases and ~500 signals; the backend has 1,206 cases (376 opened by rule per line pair), ~13,000 valid signals. The case board should show `open` + `confirmed` by default (backend default) and the Sankey needs aggregated counts (sources × car areas × cases) rather than every signal: add an aggregate endpoint or compute from `GET /cases?profile_id` (per-case `source_types`, `markets`, `distinct_customers`).
- **"Invalidate everything after a mutation"** (`hooks.ts`) re-fetches all active queries; with real data, narrow it to the affected keys if screens get slow.
- **Stale saves:** backend returns 409 when `expected_version` is old; the UI must reload the page instead of overwriting.
- **Per-vehicle actions:** every case action on the backend needs the vehicle (`/vehicles/{vehicle}/…`). Use the persona's config vehicle; Baukasten cases appear for several lines and each line decides separately.
- **Permissions differ:** backend lets any PM of one of the case's lines act; the frontend uses owner/co-owners. Until owners exist in the backend, check ownership in the adapter (sidecar) before calling.
- **Market labels:** `Rest of World` has spaces; URL-encode it in query strings.
- **Citations:** the UI's markdown turns `[ID]` into clickable links that open the signal on the case page. Backend signal ids are uuids, and the case page must be able to find them (the signals of the case must be loaded with the same ids).
- **Real data has no Chinese verbatims** for G60/G70 feedback (US-heavy). The UI says so honestly; keep that (segment chips show `China (0)`).
- **LLM keys:** backend needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the RAG agent's LLM mode and the classifier (2,557 signals still unclassified); without it the agent answers extractively with citations. The frontend's optional live features use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- **`docs/` vs `All-context/`:** the frontend branch still has `docs/` (seed script reads `docs/02-data/processed`); `main` uses `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/processed`. Point `web/scripts/seed.ts` at `All-context` when `docs/` is removed.
- **Synthetic labels:** real backend objects are not synthetic; personas, sidecar content and demo decisions are. Keep the `synthetic` flag honest in the mapping.

---

## 10. Quick reference: where to look

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| Frontend endpoint list and schemas | `web/src/contracts/api.ts`, `entities.ts`, `enums.ts` (or `contracts/openapi.yaml`) |
| Frontend business rules | `web/src/mock/handlers.ts`, `web/src/mock/scoring.ts`, `web/src/mock/ai/*` |
| Where the data source is chosen | `web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts`, `web/src/lib/api/client.ts` |
| Demo storyline and personas | `web/README.md`, `web/src/mock/authored/*` |
| Backend API guide | `backend/API.md`, `backend/app/api/routers/*.py`, `http://localhost:8000/docs` |
| Backend data model and rules | `database-design.md`, `data-model.mmd`, `CLAUDE.md` |
| Backend decisions and progress | `plan.md`, `changes.md` |
| Taxonomy | `taxonomy/README.md`, `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` |
| Meeting feedback that shaped the UI | `All-context/03-meetings-with-pm/` (Thomas demo feedback, PM interviews) |

## Context
The design phase is finished: concepts, pipeline and data model are agreed and live in `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.mmd` and `data-model.mmd`. The repo holds no code yet. Claude implements the whole backend ("the brain"); the user supervises. A teammate builds the UI (Notion-like pages, boards). The web sources are specified in `All-context/05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md` (source registry with URL patterns, categories A to J, fetch order steps 1 to 13, competitor list, slugs per site, record format). No timeline: phases are ordered by dependency and each ends in a runnable, verifiable state.

Decisions added in this round:
- **Signal** = every piece of evidence (previously "finding"). **Case** = a problem, composed of a group of signals. **Requirement** = the answer to a confirmed case.
- End filters: car area / category and **release fit** (current car update, next generation, OTA), judged by an LLM from how big the case is; the PM can override.
- **Competitor signals** (e.g. E-Class complaints, Tesla forum) attach to the BMW case of the same feature as competitor evidence; they feed the competitor gap and never count as BMW customers.
- **Fetch scope v1: steps 1 to 9** of the fetch order (reference APIs, structured APIs, news/press feeds, app reviews, forums, owner review sites, expert reviews, price lists, market/trend data). Steps 10 to 13 (native Chinese sites, browser-only, login) come later.
- **Depth:** one backfill run fetches all pages; daily runs are incremental (newest first, stop at already-stored records).
- The sources file gives URL patterns and APIs directly, so a general web-search provider is only needed for discovery (e.g. new launches); it stays pluggable.

Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Supabase (Postgres + pgvector, Storage, Realtime, Auth), OpenAI (chat + embeddings), `uv` venv, httpx + selectolax for scraping, feedparser for RSS, pdfplumber for PDFs, openpyxl/pandas inside the venv.

## Database design (built in phase 1, documented in phase 0)
Full design: [`database-design.md`](database-design.md) (diagram: `data-model.mmd`). Table groups: reference and configuration (`vehicle`, `competitor`, `source_registry`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `car_area`, `brand_profile`, `config`, `weight_profile`, `app_user`), baseline (`feature`, `feature_mapping`, `vehicle_feature`, `study_score`, `data_record` + view `sales_volume`), evidence (`agent_run`, `source_record`, `signal`), cases and requirements (`case_item`, `case_vehicle`, `case_lineage`, `case_score`, `requirement`, `page_version`), collaboration and audit (`decision`, `chat_message`, `notification`, `rag_chunk`, `audit_event`).

Changes agreed with the user in phase 0 against the first draft of this plan:
- The case table is `case_item` (`CASE` is reserved in SQL); API and UI still say "case".
- A case is not tied to one vehicle or config: one problem can apply to several BMW lines. Vehicles are tags in `case_vehicle`, which holds the per-vehicle state, PM rank, release fit, conflict flag and new-evidence flag. Case IDs are `CASE-0012`; requirements are per line (`REQ-G60-0012`, `REQ-G60-USA-0012` when split). Scores stay per weight profile, so per config.
- `car_area` is a table (the 11 car areas of the fixed taxonomy in `taxonomy/`) instead of a hard-coded list.
- Option-list pages are stored as `source_record` rows (`source_id = option_list`), so equipment facts are quotable like every other source.
- `site_slug` key includes the slug (some sites have several pages per car).

## Phase 0 — Align docs and write the database design
- `CLAUDE.md` already uses Signal and holds this round's decisions. Rename Finding → Signal in `architecture.mmd`, `data-model.mmd`, `README.md`; add "a case is composed of a group of signals", the two end filters, competitor signals, fetch scope steps 1 to 9, backfill + incremental.
- Update `data-model.mmd` to the database design above (SOURCE → `source_record`, sales folded into `data_record`, new `competitor`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `source_registry`, `feature_mapping`, `case_lineage`, `page_version`, `rag_chunk`, `notification`, `app_user`, `brand_profile`).
- Write `database-design.md` (the tables above, with rules) to the repo root. `plan.md` (this file) already exists; keep its progress table current.
- Commit `Completed phase 0: docs aligned and database design` and push.

## Context
The design phase is finished: concepts, pipeline and data model are agreed and live in `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.mmd` and `data-model.mmd`. The repo holds no code yet. Claude implements the whole backend ("the brain"); the user supervises. A teammate builds the UI (Notion-like pages, boards). The web sources are specified in `All-context/05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md` (source registry with URL patterns, categories A to J, fetch order steps 1 to 13, competitor list, slugs per site, record format). No timeline: phases are ordered by dependency and each ends in a runnable, verifiable state.

Decisions added in this round:
- **Signal** = every piece of evidence (previously "finding"). **Case** = a problem, composed of a group of signals. **Requirement** = the answer to a confirmed case.
- End filters: car area / category and **release fit** (current car update, next generation, OTA), judged by an LLM from how big the case is; the PM can override.
- **Competitor signals** (e.g. E-Class complaints, Tesla forum) attach to the BMW case of the same feature as competitor evidence; they feed the competitor gap and never count as BMW customers.
- **Fetch scope v1: steps 1 to 9** of the fetch order (reference APIs, structured APIs, news/press feeds, app reviews, forums, owner review sites, expert reviews, price lists, market/trend data). Steps 10 to 13 (native Chinese sites, browser-only, login) come later.
- **Depth:** one backfill run fetches all pages; daily runs are incremental (newest first, stop at already-stored records).
- The sources file gives URL patterns and APIs directly, so a general web-search provider is only needed for discovery (e.g. new launches); it stays pluggable.

Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Supabase (Postgres + pgvector, Storage, Realtime, Auth), OpenAI (chat + embeddings), `uv` venv, httpx + selectolax for scraping, feedparser for RSS, pdfplumber for PDFs, openpyxl/pandas inside the venv.

## Database design (built in phase 1, documented in phase 0)
Full design: [`database-design.md`](database-design.md) (diagram: `data-model.mmd`). Table groups: reference and configuration (`vehicle`, `competitor`, `source_registry`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `car_area`, `brand_profile`, `config`, `weight_profile`, `app_user`), baseline (`feature`, `feature_mapping`, `vehicle_feature`, `study_score`, `data_record` + view `sales_volume`), evidence (`agent_run`, `source_record`, `signal`), cases and requirements (`case_item`, `case_vehicle`, `case_lineage`, `case_score`, `requirement`, `page_version`), collaboration and audit (`decision`, `chat_message`, `notification`, `rag_chunk`, `audit_event`).

Changes agreed with the user in phase 0 against the first draft of this plan:
- The case table is `case_item` (`CASE` is reserved in SQL); API and UI still say "case".
- A case is not tied to one vehicle or config: one problem can apply to several BMW lines. Vehicles are tags in `case_vehicle`, which holds the per-vehicle state, PM rank, release fit, conflict flag and new-evidence flag. Case IDs are `CASE-0012`; requirements are per line (`REQ-G60-0012`, `REQ-G60-USA-0012` when split). Scores stay per weight profile, so per config.
- `car_area` is a table (the 11 car areas of the fixed taxonomy in `taxonomy/`) instead of a hard-coded list.
- Option-list pages are stored as `source_record` rows (`source_id = option_list`), so equipment facts are quotable like every other source.
- `site_slug` key includes the slug (some sites have several pages per car).

## Phase 0 — Align docs and write the database design
- `CLAUDE.md` already uses Signal and holds this round's decisions. Rename Finding → Signal in `architecture.mmd`, `data-model.mmd`, `README.md`; add "a case is composed of a group of signals", the two end filters, competitor signals, fetch scope steps 1 to 9, backfill + incremental.
- Update `data-model.mmd` to the database design above (SOURCE → `source_record`, sales folded into `data_record`, new `competitor`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `source_registry`, `feature_mapping`, `case_lineage`, `page_version`, `rag_chunk`, `notification`, `app_user`, `brand_profile`).
- Write `database-design.md` (the tables above, with rules) to the repo root. `plan.md` (this file) already exists; keep its progress table current.
- Commit `Completed phase 0: docs aligned and database design` and push.

# UI wiring plan + INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md coherence check

## Context
`INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md` (untracked, repo root) was written at ~02:30 on 2026-10-11 to connect `web/` (Next.js, own 56-endpoint contract, in-memory mock) to `backend/` (FastAPI, 53 routes). Since then: PR #5 merged, OpenAI key set, Supabase build started (HANDOFF.md). Goal: (1) list where the guide disagrees with CLAUDE.md / HANDOFF.md / plan.md / changes.md / API.md / code, (2) fix the guide, (3) plan the wiring endpoint by endpoint.

## Part A — Inconsistencies found

### A1. Guide stale vs HANDOFF.md (facts changed)
| # | Guide says | Truth (source) | Fix in guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header + §8.4 step 0: frontend on `feature/frontend-demo`, "merge PR #5" | Merged into `main` (`918ece1`; HANDOFF:23) | Drop step 0 merge; branch `feature/integration` off `main` |
| 2 | §7 + §9: OpenAI key missing, offline fallbacks | Key set in `backend/.env`; models gpt-6-luna / gpt-6.1-sol (HANDOFF:16, changes 8.12) | Say key set; RAG LLM mode on |
| 3 | §9: "2,557 signals still unclassified" | True only for the local offline build (plan.md row T). Supabase build runs the LLM classifier, so counts will change | Mark all counts as "local build, phase 10"; real numbers after Supabase build |
| 4 | §7 run: `cp .env.example .env` + `demo build --fresh` | `.env` now points at Supabase; `--fresh` is refused when `SUPABASE_DB_URL` set (demo.py:83, changes 10.1). Local needs `SUPABASE_DB_URL= SUPABASE_URL= STORAGE_BACKEND=local` prefix (HANDOFF:28) | Two run modes: local (prefix) vs Supabase (read-only for dev) |
| 5 | §8.4 step 5: run `app.demo e2e "G60 / USA"` | HANDOFF:15: never on Supabase (confirms + approves a real case; user wants PM to confirm first real case in UI). `e2e` has **no guard** in code (demo.py ~L120) | Only with local prefix; add explicit warning |
| 6 | §7 auth: `AUTH_MODE=dev` | `.env` has `AUTH_MODE` empty + `SUPABASE_URL` set ⇒ auto = `supabase` (changes 9.1). Dev header ignored | Must set `AUTH_MODE=dev` explicitly for adapter dev |
| 7 | Nothing on Realtime | HANDOFF:23, database-design:568: browser may only read `notification` via Supabase Realtime | Add: bell can subscribe to Realtime later; v1 polls `GET /notifications` |
| 8 | §2: `docs/` "older copy on the frontend branch" | Both `docs/` (57 files) and `All-context/` (60) tracked on `main`, diverged (different folder names, differing md). `web/scripts/seed.ts:6,55` reads `docs/` | Say both on main; decide: point seed at `All-context`, delete `docs/` |
| 9 | "about 50 endpoints" | 53 routes + `/health` (plan.md says 50 OpenAPI paths) | "50 paths / 53 operations" |
| 10 | Export "approved top N" | `GET /requirements/export` `top_n=10`, `format` default json (requirements.py:58) | Name the `top_n` param |

### A2. Guide ok, but CLAUDE.md / plan.md themselves stale
- CLAUDE.md "Current phase": lists OpenAI key as open, Supabase build "needs go". HANDOFF says key set, build in progress. Also "first real backfill" listed twice.
- plan.md "Open issues": "OpenAI key still missing", "Supabase build waits for user's go". Same staleness.
- changes.md 8.11 says gpt-5-mini/gpt-5, superseded by 8.12 (fine as log, but no back-reference).
→ Update CLAUDE.md + plan.md open issues (small edits).

### A3. Frontend concepts that contradict CLAUDE.md decisions (guide doesn't flag these as conflicts)
| Frontend | CLAUDE.md | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `Workspace.projectType` (`new_gen`/`lci`) in settings | **Rejected option**: "project type setting (replaced by release-fit filter)" | Must hide/remove or map to release-fit filter |
| `Case.changeDepth` (trim/part/platform/OTA) | Release fit (`current_car/next_gen/ota`) per vehicle, LLM-judged, PM override | Map changeDepth ↔ release fit, don't keep both |
| `EvidenceLevel` high/medium/low/assumption + `Signal.trust` tier | Evidence level = bmw_data/web/assumption, display only; separate confidence axis **rejected** | Adopt backend vocabulary; drop `trust` from scoring |
| `brand_fit` as a weighted factor | Multiplier fits 1.0 / neutral 0.8 / off_brand 0.5 | Follow backend (guide already recommends) |
| Case IDs `CASE-G60-0001` (vehicle in ID) | "Case IDs carry no vehicle" | Use backend IDs; contract-test IDs parametrized |
| Case lifecycle 6 states + outcomes refer/innovation/park | observed → open → confirmed/rejected per vehicle | Sub-states in sidecar = new decision → log in changes.md |
| Head of product line signs off; roles vehicle_pm/attribute_pm/head | Roles pm/engineer/admin; "PM approves; top 10 go to engineering"; **engineers edit requirements** | No engineer persona in UI; head sign-off is a new concept → decision + changes.md |
| Vehicle plan + Codebeamer CSV export | Codebeamer/Jira export = **open item / later feature** | Keep as UI-side export, mark as later scope |
| Requirement scope `global/RoW/CN` | Markets USA/China/Europe/RoW/unknown, split per market only when markets differ | Map; `RoW` ≠ "Rest of World" semantics (frontend RoW = all non-China) |
| Weight profile per user | Several per config (vehicle × market) | Follow backend |
| Chat via Anthropic (`ai/live.ts`) | OpenAI only, RAG agent with citations | Free-form chat → backend RAG |
| Scripted "research" adds synthetic web signals in chat | Signals only from fetch agents through validation gate; agents can only write signals | Disable on real data (or call predecessor-research endpoint) |

### A4. Guide internal / factual nits
- Mapping table "Market `RoW`" vs Region `RoW` — two different meanings in frontend; guide conflates.
- §1 chain "Signal → Case → Requirement → Vehicle plan → Codebeamer" vs CLAUDE.md "Signal → Case → PM confirms → Requirement → PM approves → engineering".
- §8.4 persona mapping: Wei (China 5 Series) needs a new `app_user`; demo users are created by `app.demo users` — on Supabase that is a write to real data; needs user go.
- Guide numbers (1,206 / 376 / 13,105 / 32,400 scores / 10 configs) match plan.md rows T and 10 (local build). OK but label as local.

## Part B — Wiring plan
(to be completed after backend + frontend inventories)

## 4. Plumbing

**`src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts`:**
- Lines 14-26 compile every endpoint path into a regex, turning each `:param` into `([^/]+)`.
- `match()` (lines 28-35) returns the first endpoint whose method and regex both match.
- No match returns 404 with `{error}` (line 40).
- Acting user (line 43): `x-user-id` header, then the `rs_user` cookie, then the default `"u-lena"`. A user not in the store gets a 401 (line 45).
- The query is parsed from the search params with the endpoint's Zod schema; the body is parsed from JSON, with an empty body treated as `{}` (lines 48-53).
- It then calls `handlers[name]({params, query, body, user})` from `src/mock/handlers.ts`.
- Outside production, the response is checked against the contract and only logged if it doesn't match (lines 58-61).
- Errors: a ZodError becomes 400 `{error: "Invalid request", issues}`; an `ApiError` becomes `{error}` with its own status; anything else is 500 `{error}` (lines 63-68).
- GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are all exported (line 71).

**`src/lib/api/client.ts`:**
- Base URL is `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL ?? "/api"` (line 8).
- `buildPath` (lines 26-35): replaces `:params` (URL-encoded) and throws if one is missing. It drops query values that are undefined or `""` and stringifies the rest with URLSearchParams.
- `api()` (lines 37-50):
  - Always sends `content-type: application/json`, plus `x-user-id` when the cookie is set.
  - Sends a body whenever the endpoint declares one; if the caller passes none, it sends `{}`.
  - On a non-2xx response it throws `ApiRequestError(status, json.error ?? "Request failed (N)", json.issues)`. The backend error shape the UI expects is therefore `{error: string, issues?}`.

## 2. Auth, CORS, errors
- **`current_user`** (`api/auth.py:77-86`):
  - `AUTH_MODE=dev`: needs the `X-User-Id: <uuid>` header. A missing header gives 401.
  - Otherwise: needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
  - Tokens are verified with HS256 and `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`, or with JWKS (RS256/ES256), audience `authenticated`. The `sub` claim is the user id (`:47-62`).
  - The user must exist in `app_user`: a non-uuid id gives 401, an unknown user gives 403 (`:65-74`).
  - The actor string is `"{role}:{id}"`.
- **Mode selection**: `auth_mode` defaults to `"auto"`, which becomes `supabase` if `SUPABASE_URL` is set, else `dev` (`config.py:31,80-81`).
- **CORS**: `CORS_ORIGINS`, default exactly `http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:5173` (`config.py:34`). `.env` and `.env.example` hold the same value. Credentials are allowed, methods and headers are `*`, and `x-request-id` is exposed (`main.py:19-23`).
- **Request id**: the `x-request-id` header is echoed back, or generated if missing (`deps.py:31-40`).
- **Error format**: `{"detail": "<string>"}` for `HTTPException` and the mapped exceptions (`deps.py:42-51`):
  - `NotFound` → 404
  - `StaleVersion`, `InvalidTransition`, `InvalidAction` → 409
  - any other `ValueError` → 422
  - Pydantic validation errors use FastAPI's default `{"detail": [{loc, msg, type, …}]}`.
  - Unmapped DB errors return a 500.
- **Transactions**: one per request, so audit rows commit together with the change (`deps.py:23-27`).

  - `…0003` "Demo PM 1 Series", pm, `[F70]`
  - `…0004` "Demo engineer", engineer, `[]`
  - `…0005` "Demo admin", admin, `[]`
  - The full id prefix is `00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000N`.
- **Configs**: one per current vehicle × market with 2030 sales above 0, named `"{code} / {market}"` (`seed/run.py:114-130`; markets_sold set in `seed/loaders.py:76-83`). From the sales README that gives 10 configs, which matches plan.md:
  - F70: Europe, Rest of World
  - G60: USA, China, Europe, Rest of World
  - G70: USA, China, Europe, Rest of World
  - I took this list from the docs and reports, not by querying the database.
- **Weight profiles**: 4 per config (`seed/run.py:18-29`). Base weights:

  | Factor | Weight |
  |---|---|
  | distinct_customers | 0.25 |
  | severity | 0.20 |
  | satisfaction_gap | 0.15 |
  | competitor_gap | 0.15 |
  | market_volume | 0.10 |
  | removed_vs_predecessor | 0.05 |
  | reach | 0.05 |
  | trend | 0.05 |

  | Profile | Weights | Cost multipliers S / M / L | Default |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `balanced` | base weights | 1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 | yes |
  | `customer voice` | base, with distinct_customers .35, severity .25, competitor_gap .05, market_volume .05, trend 0 | 1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 | no |

    - in_discussion ← draft
    - approved ← draft, in_discussion

### A5. Found while mapping the code (missing from the guide)
- **Admin cannot approve.** The guide maps Katrin (head) to `…0005` admin. But `requirements/service.py:52` only accepts `pm:` actors for `approved`, so an admin gets a 409.
- **No user with all lines.** The guide maps Jonas to "a PM with all lines", and Wei to a second G60 PM. No such `app_user` rows exist. They must be created (`vehicles = []` means all lines).
- **Errors need translating.** Backend errors are `{detail}`, and a 422 is `{detail:[…]}`. The UI reads `{error, issues}`.
- **`GET /cases` needs `profile_id`, and the UI board calls `cases` with no query.** The adapter must take the profile from the workspace. The board defaults to `open+confirmed`, but the UI kanban has an `observed` column, so it must request `state=observed` too. That is about 1,200 rows per line, with no pagination.
- **Chat citations are bare uuids.** `cited_signals` holds signal uuids only. Labels need the signal rows.
- **Requirement fields differ in shape:**
  - `metric_target` is one object `{metric,today,target,competitor_reference}`; the UI expects `Metric[]`.
  - The list rows lack the description, metrics and acceptance criteria.
- **Brand profile save needs a rationale.** The backend uses POST with `{body_md, rationale}`; the UI's PUT sends no rationale.
- **`readNotifications` with no ids means "all".** The backend marks one at a time and has no "read all".
- **`reopen` also works from `confirmed`** on the backend. The guide lists only open/confirm/reject.

## Part B — Wiring plan (Next.js adapter, Supabase target)

### B0. Decisions taken
- **Adapter:** BFF inside Next.js (user).
- **Data:** Supabase directly (user). Consequence:
  - Every confirm, approve or merge click during development is permanent in the append-only audit log. That covers the "PM confirms first real case in UI" wish, but test clicks pollute it.
  - Mitigation: wire and verify the read paths first. Write paths get click-tested on one agreed case only, and `contract-test` write steps are skipped against Supabase.
- **Missing features:** sidecar first (recommended, decided for the user as most feasible).
  - A persisted JSON sidecar (`web/.data/sidecar.json`), keyed by backend IDs, so state survives restarts.
  - Promote to backend tables after the demo, in this order: questions, referrals, comments, sign-off statuses.

entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

# UI wiring plan + INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md coherence check

## Context
`INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md` (untracked, repo root) was written at ~02:30 on 2026-10-11 to connect `web/` (Next.js, own 56-endpoint contract, in-memory mock) to `backend/` (FastAPI, 53 routes). Since then: PR #5 merged, OpenAI key set, Supabase build started (HANDOFF.md). Goal: (1) list where the guide disagrees with CLAUDE.md / HANDOFF.md / plan.md / changes.md / API.md / code, (2) fix the guide, (3) plan the wiring endpoint by endpoint.

## Part A — Inconsistencies found

### A1. Guide stale vs HANDOFF.md (facts changed)
| # | Guide says | Truth (source) | Fix in guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Header + §8.4 step 0: frontend on `feature/frontend-demo`, "merge PR #5" | Merged into `main` (`918ece1`; HANDOFF:23) | Drop step 0 merge; branch `feature/integration` off `main` |
| 2 | §7 + §9: OpenAI key missing, offline fallbacks | Key set in `backend/.env`; models gpt-6-luna / gpt-6.1-sol (HANDOFF:16, changes 8.12) | Say key set; RAG LLM mode on |
| 3 | §9: "2,557 signals still unclassified" | True only for the local offline build (plan.md row T). Supabase build runs the LLM classifier, so counts will change | Mark all counts as "local build, phase 10"; real numbers after Supabase build |
| 4 | §7 run: `cp .env.example .env` + `demo build --fresh` | `.env` now points at Supabase; `--fresh` is refused when `SUPABASE_DB_URL` set (demo.py:83, changes 10.1). Local needs `SUPABASE_DB_URL= SUPABASE_URL= STORAGE_BACKEND=local` prefix (HANDOFF:28) | Two run modes: local (prefix) vs Supabase (read-only for dev) |
| 5 | §8.4 step 5: run `app.demo e2e "G60 / USA"` | HANDOFF:15: never on Supabase (confirms + approves a real case; user wants PM to confirm first real case in UI). `e2e` has **no guard** in code (demo.py ~L120) | Only with local prefix; add explicit warning |
| 6 | §7 auth: `AUTH_MODE=dev` | `.env` has `AUTH_MODE` empty + `SUPABASE_URL` set ⇒ auto = `supabase` (changes 9.1). Dev header ignored | Must set `AUTH_MODE=dev` explicitly for adapter dev |
| 7 | Nothing on Realtime | HANDOFF:23, database-design:568: browser may only read `notification` via Supabase Realtime | Add: bell can subscribe to Realtime later; v1 polls `GET /notifications` |
| 8 | §2: `docs/` "older copy on the frontend branch" | Both `docs/` (57 files) and `All-context/` (60) tracked on `main`, diverged (different folder names, differing md). `web/scripts/seed.ts:6,55` reads `docs/` | Say both on main; decide: point seed at `All-context`, delete `docs/` |
| 9 | "about 50 endpoints" | 53 routes + `/health` (plan.md says 50 OpenAPI paths) | "50 paths / 53 operations" |
| 10 | Export "approved top N" | `GET /requirements/export` `top_n=10`, `format` default json (requirements.py:58) | Name the `top_n` param |

### A2. Guide ok, but CLAUDE.md / plan.md themselves stale
- CLAUDE.md "Current phase": lists OpenAI key as open, Supabase build "needs go". HANDOFF says key set, build in progress. Also "first real backfill" listed twice.
- plan.md "Open issues": "OpenAI key still missing", "Supabase build waits for user's go". Same staleness.
- changes.md 8.11 says gpt-5-mini/gpt-5, superseded by 8.12 (fine as log, but no back-reference).
→ Update CLAUDE.md + plan.md open issues (small edits).

### A3. Frontend concepts that contradict CLAUDE.md decisions (guide doesn't flag these as conflicts)
| Frontend | CLAUDE.md | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `Workspace.projectType` (`new_gen`/`lci`) in settings | **Rejected option**: "project type setting (replaced by release-fit filter)" | Must hide/remove or map to release-fit filter |
| `Case.changeDepth` (trim/part/platform/OTA) | Release fit (`current_car/next_gen/ota`) per vehicle, LLM-judged, PM override | Map changeDepth ↔ release fit, don't keep both |
| `EvidenceLevel` high/medium/low/assumption + `Signal.trust` tier | Evidence level = bmw_data/web/assumption, display only; separate confidence axis **rejected** | Adopt backend vocabulary; drop `trust` from scoring |
| `brand_fit` as a weighted factor | Multiplier fits 1.0 / neutral 0.8 / off_brand 0.5 | Follow backend (guide already recommends) |
| Case IDs `CASE-G60-0001` (vehicle in ID) | "Case IDs carry no vehicle" | Use backend IDs; contract-test IDs parametrized |
| Case lifecycle 6 states + outcomes refer/innovation/park | observed → open → confirmed/rejected per vehicle | Sub-states in sidecar = new decision → log in changes.md |
| Head of product line signs off; roles vehicle_pm/attribute_pm/head | Roles pm/engineer/admin; "PM approves; top 10 go to engineering"; **engineers edit requirements** | No engineer persona in UI; head sign-off is a new concept → decision + changes.md |
| Vehicle plan + Codebeamer CSV export | Codebeamer/Jira export = **open item / later feature** | Keep as UI-side export, mark as later scope |
| Requirement scope `global/RoW/CN` | Markets USA/China/Europe/RoW/unknown, split per market only when markets differ | Map; `RoW` ≠ "Rest of World" semantics (frontend RoW = all non-China) |
| Weight profile per user | Several per config (vehicle × market) | Follow backend |
| Chat via Anthropic (`ai/live.ts`) | OpenAI only, RAG agent with citations | Free-form chat → backend RAG |
| Scripted "research" adds synthetic web signals in chat | Signals only from fetch agents through validation gate; agents can only write signals | Disable on real data (or call predecessor-research endpoint) |

### A4. Guide internal / factual nits
- Mapping table "Market `RoW`" vs Region `RoW` — two different meanings in frontend; guide conflates.
- §1 chain "Signal → Case → Requirement → Vehicle plan → Codebeamer" vs CLAUDE.md "Signal → Case → PM confirms → Requirement → PM approves → engineering".
- §8.4 persona mapping: Wei (China 5 Series) needs a new `app_user`; demo users are created by `app.demo users` — on Supabase that is a write to real data; needs user go.
- Guide numbers (1,206 / 376 / 13,105 / 32,400 scores / 10 configs) match plan.md rows T and 10 (local build). OK but label as local.

### A5. Found while mapping the code (missing from the guide)
- **Admin cannot approve.** The guide maps Katrin (head) to `…0005` admin. But `requirements/service.py:52` only accepts `pm:` actors for `approved`, so an admin gets a 409.
- **No user with all lines.** The guide maps Jonas to "a PM with all lines", and Wei to a second G60 PM. No such `app_user` rows exist. They must be created (`vehicles = []` means all lines).
- **Errors need translating.** Backend errors are `{detail}`, and a 422 is `{detail:[…]}`. The UI reads `{error, issues}`.
- **`GET /cases` needs `profile_id`, and the UI board calls `cases` with no query.** The adapter must take the profile from the workspace. The board defaults to `open+confirmed`, but the UI kanban has an `observed` column, so it must request `state=observed` too. That is about 1,200 rows per line, with no pagination.
- **Chat citations are bare uuids.** `cited_signals` holds signal uuids only. Labels need the signal rows.
- **Requirement fields differ in shape:**
  - `metric_target` is one object `{metric,today,target,competitor_reference}`; the UI expects `Metric[]`.
  - The list rows lack the description, metrics and acceptance criteria.
- **Brand profile save needs a rationale.** The backend uses POST with `{body_md, rationale}`; the UI's PUT sends no rationale.
- **`readNotifications` with no ids means "all".** The backend marks one at a time and has no "read all".
- **`reopen` also works from `confirmed`** on the backend. The guide lists only open/confirm/reject.

## Part B — Wiring plan (Next.js adapter, Supabase target)

### B0. Decisions taken
- **Adapter:** BFF inside Next.js (user).
- **Data:** Supabase directly (user). Consequence:
  - Every confirm, approve or merge click during development is permanent in the append-only audit log. That covers the "PM confirms first real case in UI" wish, but test clicks pollute it.
  - Mitigation: wire and verify the read paths first. Write paths get click-tested on one agreed case only, and `contract-test` write steps are skipped against Supabase.
- **Missing features:** sidecar first (recommended, decided for the user as most feasible).
  - A persisted JSON sidecar (`web/.data/sidecar.json`), keyed by backend IDs, so state survives restarts.
  - Promote to backend tables after the demo, in this order: questions, referrals, comments, sign-off statuses.
  - Reason: it needs no migration on the live Supabase, and it reuses the mock logic as-is.
- **Preconditions (need user go, they write to Supabase):**
  1. The Supabase build is finished (`agent_run` last rows ok).
  2. Demo users exist on Supabase (`app.demo users`), plus 2 extra `app_user` rows: an all-lines PM for Jonas, and a G60 PM for Wei.
  3. `backend/.env` has `AUTH_MODE=dev` for local API runs.

### B1. Plumbing (new folder `web/src/backend/`)
- **`client.ts`:**
  - Server-side `fetch(BACKEND_URL + path)` with header `X-User-Id` (persona → uuid map).
  - Repeats array query params (`state=open&state=confirmed`).
  - Maps `{detail}` to `ApiError(status, msg)`.
- **`map.ts`:** pure, unit-tested vocabulary maps, both directions:
  - market, region↔market, release `lci↔current_car`, evidence level, factors (`customers↔distinct_customers`, `regression↔removed_vs_predecessor`, +`reach`, brand_fit = multiplier), cost source `finance↔engineering`
  - requirement status (backend `approved` + sidecar layer for `pm_approved` / `signed_off` / `planned` / `exported`)
  - case state (backend observed/open/confirmed/rejected + sidecar sub-state and outcome)
  - `changeDepth ↔ release_fit`
- **`personas.ts`:**

  | Persona | Backend user | Config |
  |---|---|---|
  | Lena | `…0001` | G60 / USA |
  | Wei | new G60 PM | G60 / China |
  | Sofia | `…0003` | F70 / Europe |
  | Daniel | `…0002` | G70 / USA |
  | Jonas | new all-lines PM | G60 / Europe |
  | Katrin (head) | the same all-lines PM row as Jonas (an admin cannot approve) | G60 / USA |

  Head-only actions (sign-off, send back, resolve) live in the sidecar.
- **`sidecar.ts`:** reuse the `mock/store.ts` helpers (`audit`, `notify`, `nextId`) over a JSON-file store.
  - Covers: questions, meeting notes, pmContext, referrals, innovation meta, comments, alerts, plan features, proposals (non-diff kinds), quality checks, the case sub-state/outcome/owner/watchers, and the requirement sign-off layer.
  - Sidecar audit events are merged into the `audit` responses, tagged `synthetic`.
- **`handlers.ts`:** `Partial<Handlers>` with the same signatures as `mock/handlers.ts`.
- **`route.ts`:** if `DATA_SOURCE=backend`, use `backendHandlers[name] ?? mockHandlers[name]`, and resolve the user from `personas.ts` instead of the mock store.
- **Caching:** per-request memo for `/configs`, `/taxonomy`, and per-profile boards (15 s), to keep N+1 calls cheap.

### B2. Endpoint map (all 56)
Legend: **B** = backend call, **S** = sidecar, **B+S** = backend + sidecar overlay, **A** = computed in the adapter from backend data.

| Frontend | How | Backend calls / notes |
|---|---|---|
| me | B+S | `GET /me` + `GET /configs` → workspace (config, default profile) + profile |
| users | A | static persona list from `personas.ts` |
| updateWorkspace | S | switch config/profile. Source filter → `PATCH /configs/{id}` (rationale auto). `projectType` hidden (rejected option) |
| search | A | board `q` on the current profile + requirement list + persona names |
| signals | B | `GET /signals` (`vehicle`, `case_id`, `market`, `kind`, `limit≤500`); agent from `evidence_role`/`content_type`; `trust` dropped from the UI |
| clusters | — | unused by the UI; return `[]` |
| agentRuns | B | `GET /runs` |
| refresh | B (stub) | no trigger endpoint: return the latest runs, plus a toast "the daily worker runs on cron" |
| quarantine | B | `GET /quarantine` items |
| cases | B+S | `GET /cases?profile_id&state=observed&state=open&state=confirmed&state=rejected` → Case; owner/sub-state from S |
| createCase | B | `POST /cases/{seed}/split {signal_ids}` (same topic only; else 422 → toast) |
| caseBundle | B+S | `GET /cases/{id}` + `GET /signals?case_id&limit=500` + `GET /requirements/{rid}` for each linked requirement + S (questions, referrals, alerts, notes, proposals) |
| patchCase | B+S | title/bodyMd → `PUT /cases/{id}/page` (version, 409 → reload); brandFit → `POST /tags`; manualRank → `POST /vehicles/{v}/rank`; watchers/co-owners → S |
| transitionCase | B+S | open/confirm/reject/reopen → `POST /vehicles/{v}/transition`; merge → `POST /merge`; start/await/ready/refer/innovation/park → S |
| createQuestion, questions, patchQuestion | S | |
| addMeetingNote | S | reuse `mock/ai/notes.ts` |
| savePmContext | S | follow-up via scripted `ai/chat.ts` |
| generateRequirements | B | `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{v}/requirements`, then fetch each requirement |
| exportCaseMd | A | from `body_md` + figures |
| caseSegments | A | port `mock/ai/segment.ts` over the case signals with `evidence_role=bmw_customer` |
| requirements | B+S | `GET /requirements?profile_id&status=…` + `GET /requirements/{id}` per row (few rows) |
| requirementBundle | B+S | `GET /requirements/{id}` + caseBundle parts + S (check, plan feature) |
| patchRequirement | B | releaseTarget → `/retarget`; cost → `/cost`; manualRank → `/rank`; title/description/metrics/criteria/assumptions → render into `body_md` → `PUT /page` (decision 4 in the guide still open) |
| transitionRequirement | B+S | discuss → `in_discussion`; approve → `approved`; reject → `rejected`; restore → `draft`; send_back → `in_discussion` + S reason; sign_off/plan/export → S layer |
| runRequirementCheck | A | `mock/ai/quality.ts` on mapped data |
| scores | A | board rows (score, rank) + factors from `GET /cases/{id}` for the top N only (lazy) |
| previewScores | A | recompute `brand × Σw·f/Σw` from cached factor values |
| weightProfiles | B | profiles of the persona config (`GET /configs/{id}`) |
| saveWeightProfile | B | `PATCH /profiles/{id}` |
| createWeightProfile | B | `POST /configs/{id}/profiles` |
| brandProfile / saveBrandProfile | B | `body_md` ↔ notesMd; pillars/doNot parsed from md headings; rationale auto-filled |
| referrals, decideReferral | S | accept → linked case = S link to the same backend case for the receiver's line |
| innovation, voteInnovation, pullInnovation | S | |
| plan | A+S | equipment from `figures.by_vehicle[v].equipment` of the plan's cases; actions from S |
| patchPlanFeature | S | |
| exportRequirements | A | Codebeamer CSV in the UI columns from mapped requirements (the backend export logs only the approved top N; also call it so the export is logged) |
| requirementDeck | A | from requirement + case factors + signals + decisions |
| messages | B+S | `GET /chat/{type}/{id}` + S scripted messages, merged by time |
| postMessage | B / A | free text → `POST /chat` (RAG, OpenAI); `[signal:uuid]` → `[uuid]` + citations from signals; scripted intents (draft requirement, questions, segment) → A |
| decideProposal | B / S | body diff → `POST /chat/messages/{id}/decision`; other kinds → S |
| comments, addComment | S | |
| notifications | B+S | `GET /notifications` mapped + S notifications |
| readNotifications | B | loop `POST /notifications/{id}/read` (all unread if no ids) |
| alerts, resolveAlert | S | seed alerts from backend notifications of type `new_competitor` / `market_conflict` |
| audit | B+S | with objectId → `GET /audit/{type}/{id}`; global → S events + audit of the user's recent objects (no backend global list) |
| taxonomy | B | map field names |
| portfolio | — | unused by the UI; return a minimal response |
| reset | S | reset the sidecar only, never the backend |

### B3. Order of work
1. **Doc fixes** (Part A):
   - `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`: A1, A3, A4, A5, plus the Supabase-direct choice.
   - CLAUDE.md "Current phase" and plan.md "Open issues": OpenAI key set, Supabase build in progress.
2. **Plumbing:** client, map + tests, personas, sidecar, route switch, `.env.local` (`DATA_SOURCE`, `BACKEND_URL`).
3. **Read paths:** me, taxonomy, configs/profiles, cases board, caseBundle, signals, requirements, scores, notifications, runs, quarantine, audit.
4. **AI:** chat read/post/decision (RAG), segments, quality check.
5. **Write paths:** transitions, page saves, tags/rank, requirement status/cost/retarget, profiles.
6. **Sidecar features:** questions, notes, referrals, innovation, comments, alerts, plan, deck, export.
7. **Contract-test:** parametrize the IDs (pick from the board), plus a `READ_ONLY=1` mode for Supabase.

### B4. Critical files
- Modify: `web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts`, `web/scripts/contract-test.ts`, `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `plan.md`.
- New: `web/src/backend/{client,map,personas,sidecar,handlers}.ts`, `web/.env.local` (not committed).
- Reuse: `web/src/mock/store.ts` (audit/notify helpers), `web/src/mock/ai/{segment,quality,notes,chat,drafts}.ts`, `web/src/mock/scoring.ts` (preview formula, adjusted to the multiplier), `web/src/lib/deck.ts`.

## Verification
- Run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` in `web/`.
- Unit tests for `map.ts`: round trip of every vocabulary.
- Run `uvicorn` with `AUTH_MODE=dev` against Supabase, and `npm run dev` with `DATA_SOURCE=backend`.
- `API_BASE=http://localhost:3000/api READ_ONLY=1 npm run contract-test`: every response passes Zod.
- Click through: login (Lena) → board shows real G60 / USA cases → case page Sankey with real quotes → chat answer cites real signals → audit tab shows `pm:<uuid>` events.
- One agreed write test on Supabase: confirm 1 case → requirement appears → status discuss.
- `DATA_SOURCE=mock` still passes the full contract-test (fallback intact).

  |---|---|---|
  | Lena | `…0001` | G60 / USA |
  | Wei | new G60 PM | G60 / China |
  | Sofia | `…0003` | F70 / Europe |
  | Daniel | `…0002` | G70 / USA |
  | Jonas | new all-lines PM | G60 / Europe |
  | Katrin (head) | the same all-lines PM row as Jonas (an admin cannot approve) | G60 / USA |

| savePmContext | S | follow-up via scripted `ai/chat.ts` |
| generateRequirements | B | `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{v}/requirements`, then fetch each requirement |
| exportCaseMd | A | from `body_md` + figures |
| caseSegments | A | port `mock/ai/segment.ts` over the case signals with `evidence_role=bmw_customer` |

| weightProfiles | B | profiles of the persona config (`GET /configs/{id}`) |

| createWeightProfile | B | `POST /configs/{id}/profiles` |
| brandProfile / saveBrandProfile | B | `body_md` ↔ notesMd; pillars/doNot parsed from md headings; rationale auto-filled |
| referrals, decideReferral | S | accept → linked case = S link to the same backend case for the receiver's line |
| innovation, voteInnovation, pullInnovation | S | |

| patchPlanFeature | S | |

| comments, addComment | S | |
| notifications | B+S | `GET /notifications` mapped + S notifications |
| readNotifications | B | loop `POST /notifications/{id}/read` (all unread if no ids) |
| alerts, resolveAlert | S | seed alerts from backend notifications of type `new_competitor` / `market_conflict` |
| audit | B+S | with objectId → `GET /audit/{type}/{id}`; global → S events + audit of the user's recent objects (no backend global list) |
| taxonomy | B | map field names |
| portfolio | — | unused by the UI; return a minimal response |
| reset | S | reset the sidecar only, never the backend |

### B3. Order of work
1. **Doc fixes** (Part A):
   - `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`: A1, A3, A4, A5, plus the Supabase-direct choice.
   - CLAUDE.md "Current phase" and plan.md "Open issues": OpenAI key set, Supabase build in progress.
2. **Plumbing:** client, map + tests, personas, sidecar, route switch, `.env.local` (`DATA_SOURCE`, `BACKEND_URL`).
3. **Read paths:** me, taxonomy, configs/profiles, cases board, caseBundle, signals, requirements, scores, notifications, runs, quarantine, audit.
4. **AI:** chat read/post/decision (RAG), segments, quality check.
5. **Write paths:** transitions, page saves, tags/rank, requirement status/cost/retarget, profiles.
6. **Sidecar features:** questions, notes, referrals, innovation, comments, alerts, plan, deck, export.
7. **Contract-test:** parametrize the IDs (pick from the board), plus a `READ_ONLY=1` mode for Supabase.

- Modify: `web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts`, `web/scripts/contract-test.ts`, `INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `plan.md`.

- Unit tests for `map.ts`: round trip of every vocabulary.
- Run `uvicorn` with `AUTH_MODE=dev` against Supabase, and `npm run dev` with `DATA_SOURCE=backend`.
- `API_BASE=http://localhost:3000/api READ_ONLY=1 npm run contract-test`: every response passes Zod.

- `DATA_SOURCE=mock` still passes the full contract-test (fallback intact).

-## Context

-The design phase is finished: concepts, pipeline and data model are agreed and live in `CLAUDE.md`, `architecture.mmd` and `data-model.mmd`. The repo holds no code yet. Claude implements the whole backend ("the brain"); the user supervises. A teammate builds the UI (Notion-like pages, boards). The web sources are specified in `All-context/05-web-sources/fetching-sources.md` (source registry with URL patterns, categories A to J, fetch order steps 1 to 13, competitor list, slugs per site, record format). No timeline: phases are ordered by dependency and each ends in a runnable, verifiable state.
-Decisions added in this round:
-- **Signal** = every piece of evidence (previously "finding"). **Case** = a problem, composed of a group of signals. **Requirement** = the answer to a confirmed case.
-- End filters: car area / category and **release fit** (current car update, next generation, OTA), judged by an LLM from how big the case is; the PM can override.
-- **Competitor signals** (e.g. E-Class complaints, Tesla forum) attach to the BMW case of the same feature as competitor evidence; they feed the competitor gap and never count as BMW customers.

-- **Fetch scope v1: steps 1 to 9** of the fetch order (reference APIs, structured APIs, news/press feeds, app reviews, forums, owner review sites, expert reviews, price lists, market/trend data). Steps 10 to 13 (native Chinese sites, browser-only, login) come later.
-- **Depth:** one backfill run fetches all pages; daily runs are incremental (newest first, stop at already-stored records).
-- The sources file gives URL patterns and APIs directly, so a general web-search provider is only needed for discovery (e.g. new launches); it stays pluggable.

-Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Supabase (Postgres + pgvector, Storage, Realtime, Auth), OpenAI (chat + embeddings), `uv` venv, httpx + selectolax for scraping, feedparser for RSS, pdfplumber for PDFs, openpyxl/pandas inside the venv.
-## Database design (built in phase 1, documented in phase 0)

-Full design: [`database-design.md`](database-design.md) (diagram: `data-model.mmd`). Table groups: reference and configuration (`vehicle`, `competitor`, `source_registry`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `car_area`, `brand_profile`, `config`, `weight_profile`, `app_user`), baseline (`feature`, `feature_mapping`, `vehicle_feature`, `study_score`, `data_record` + view `sales_volume`), evidence (`agent_run`, `source_record`, `signal`), cases and requirements (`case_item`, `case_vehicle`, `case_lineage`, `case_score`, `requirement`, `page_version`), collaboration and audit (`decision`, `chat_message`, `notification`, `rag_chunk`, `audit_event`).
-Changes agreed with the user in phase 0 against the first draft of this plan:
-- The case table is `case_item` (`CASE` is reserved in SQL); API and UI still say "case".

-- A case is not tied to one vehicle or config: one problem can apply to several BMW lines. Vehicles are tags in `case_vehicle`, which holds the per-vehicle state, PM rank, release fit, conflict flag and new-evidence flag. Case IDs are `CASE-0012`; requirements are per line (`REQ-G60-0012`, `REQ-G60-USA-0012` when split). Scores stay per weight profile, so per config.
-- `car_area` is a table (the 11 car areas of the fixed taxonomy in `taxonomy/`) instead of a hard-coded list.
-- Option-list pages are stored as `source_record` rows (`source_id = option_list`), so equipment facts are quotable like every other source.
-- `site_slug` key includes the slug (some sites have several pages per car).
-## Phase 0 — Align docs and write the database design

-- `CLAUDE.md` already uses Signal and holds this round's decisions. Rename Finding → Signal in `architecture.mmd`, `data-model.mmd`, `README.md`; add "a case is composed of a group of signals", the two end filters, competitor signals, fetch scope steps 1 to 9, backfill + incremental.

-- Update `data-model.mmd` to the database design above (SOURCE → `source_record`, sales folded into `data_record`, new `competitor`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, `source_registry`, `feature_mapping`, `case_lineage`, `page_version`, `rag_chunk`, `notification`, `app_user`, `brand_profile`).
-- Write `database-design.md` (the tables above, with rules) to the repo root. `plan.md` (this file) already exists; keep its progress table current.
-- Commit `Completed phase 0: docs aligned and database design` and push.
-## Phase 1 — Foundation
-- `backend/` skeleton: `uv` project, FastAPI app, `config.py` (pydantic-settings), `db.py` (psycopg pool + Supabase storage client), `.env.example` (keys never committed).
-- `backend/supabase/migrations/`: one migration per table group above, extensions (`vector`), indexes, append-only trigger on `audit_event`, Realtime on `notification`, storage bucket `raw-records`.
-- `audit.py`: `write(object_type, object_id, before, after, actor, rationale)` in the same transaction as the change; actors `seed:<script>`, `agent:<name>`, `pm:<user>`, `system`.
-- `llm/`: OpenAI wrapper with structured outputs (JSON schema), retries, cost logging; `prompts/` as versioned files.
-- Test: update/delete on `audit_event` fails.
-## Phase 2 — Seed

-- Pre-seeding: everything in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/` (3 feedback files, customer study, sales volumes, 3 option-list PDFs) is imported into the tables created in phase 1, read-only from `raw/`, each file also stored in the `raw-records` bucket.
-- **Registry seed** (parse `fetching-sources.md` once into YAML, reviewed, then load): `source_registry`, `competitor`, `site_slug`, `search_term`, vehicle generations / `on_sale_since`.
-- **Portfolio** → `vehicle`. **Sales** → `data_record` (identical RoW values flagged `suspect`).

-- **Fixed taxonomy** (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`, not reviewed in the seed; only a human changes it in `taxonomy/`): 11 car areas → `car_area`, 11 aspect groups → `aspect_group`, 219 topics plus the fallback `other` → `feature` (one row per topic, `feature.topic_id`), BMW's VFC level-2 labels and aliases → `feature_mapping`.
-- **Study** → `study_score` (CN_EU means normalized; US distributions → normalized mean + dissatisfied share), linked to topics through the review CSV `study_attributes.csv`.

-- **BMW feedback** → `source_record` per verbatim ID + one `signal` per topic row (kind/severity from Feedback Type, market via fetching-sources 7.4, `BEVE` → `BEV`, source C prefix stripped, `evidence_role = bmw_customer`). Topic and aspect group by lookup from the VFC level-2 and level-3 labels (`classified_by = bmw_label`); the car area is derived from the topic. Aspect group `price` is tagged out of scope.

-- Rows the labels cannot place are classified from the text by the LLM (`feedback_classify@v2`, closed lists): rows without a Feedback Type (kind/severity) and rows labelled `no_class_found` or general enquiry (topic and aspect group).
